Aurora Research Notes — Local Knowledge Base Fixture

The Aurora satellite constellation uses low-Earth-orbit relays to deliver
sub-second telemetry to ground stations. Each satellite carries a radiation-
hardened SQLite archive that stores the last 72 hours of sensor readings
offline when ground contact is lost.

Key finding (2024): when the constellation switches to store-and-forward mode,
packet loss drops from 4.2% to 0.8%, but end-to-end latency rises from 180ms
to roughly 2.5 seconds. Engineers recommend enabling store-and-forward only
during solar-flare blackouts.

The project codename for the onboard database module is "Nimbus Cache".
Nimbus Cache checkpoints every 90 seconds and can rebuild indexes after a
sudden power brownout within 12 seconds.
